text: so basically a DID is like a phone number that nobody gave you. you create it yourself, nobody owns it, and nobody can take it away. someone sends you a message signed by their DID. you take the DID, extract the public key, and verify the signature. if it checks out, that person really sent it.

you can have unlimited DIDs. one for work, one for personal stuff, one for anonymous browsing. nobody can link them unless you choose to. traditional identity systems like google or facebook accounts are custodial. they hold your identity for you. DID flips this completely. you hold your own keys.

DID authentication works by challenging the holder to sign something with their private key. if the signature matches the public key in the DID document youre in. think about your email address right now. gmail owns that. they can delete it, block it, whatever. a DID is different because YOU control it completely.
